title: Principality of Terebovlia
capsule: The Principality of Terebovlia was a Rus' appanage centred on the fortress town of Terebovlia in southeastern Galicia, granted to Vasylko Rostyslavych around 1085 as part of the territorial settlement among the Rostyslavych princes. Vasylko was an energetic frontier administrator who settled Berendey, Tork, and Pecheneg auxiliaries along the southeastern marches to defend against nomadic incursion; his blinding by Davyd Ihorevych in 1097, described in detail by the Primary Chronicle, triggered a Rus' inter-princely war. After Vasylko's death in 1124 the principality passed to his son Rostyslav; by 1141 Volodymyrko Volodarovych consolidated Terebovlia along with Peremyshl and Zvenyhorod into the united Principality of Galicia.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The principality's core around Terebovlia is established from chronicle accounts; outer boundaries and precise extent fluctuated with Rus' dynastic politics and are only approximately known.
